public_rationale: Open Terms Archive documented a January 16, 2026 Starlink policy change permitting AI training and requiring users to opt out of third-party training [e1]. Anthropic's August 28, 2025 announcement said existing users would see a training choice in a pop-up window [e2]. These records establish neither a broad, repeated pattern of default training use with obscure disclosure nor a decisive development ruling that pattern out [e1, e2].
limitations: Starlink's policy permissions do not establish actual training use or the visibility of notices to affected users.
Anthropic's announcement describes its planned user-choice process, not independently verified delivery or user understanding.
The evidence does not establish prevalence across companies and services.
The forecast supplies no deadline or numerical threshold for 'a lot.'

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Covert opt-out scraping of user data for AI training will happen a lot.

statement.excerpt: Be on your guard; it’s going to happen a lot.
statement.document_title: PSA: Microsoft may be training on your private data without your knowledge

from_speaker: it’s going to happen a lot
hiding what is going in obscure settings and Terms of Service
our_interpretation: It refers to the preceding prediction of concealed default inclusion of user data in AI training.
A lot means a recurrent, widespread practice across companies and services, rather than an isolated case.
No numerical count, market share, frequency, or deadline is supplied. I do not invent one.
Be on your guard is advice and is not itself graded.
criteria.support_condition: Dated evidence establishes a broad, repeated post-publication pattern of companies using default inclusion for AI training while leaving material disclosure and opt-outs obscure.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A decisive development rules out the predicted widespread recurrence. A limited number of examples or a period without examples cannot refute an undated forecast.

evidence.explanation: The policy monitor documents training permissions and an opt-out requirement for third-party training. One observed policy change cannot establish widespread covert training or actual use of the data.

evidence.locator: Paragraph describing how new and existing users select their preference
evidence.explanation: Anthropic describes presenting the training choice directly to existing users. This challenges counting its policy change as evidence of a concealed practice, but cannot refute a forecast about other companies.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A dated cross-company investigation or substantial collection of verified records establishing a broad, repeated post-publication pattern of default inclusion in AI training with obscure notices and opt-outs; alternatively, a decisive development ruling out the predicted recurrence.
